The code uses `workingHours.find()` to search for a working hour interval where the slot is OUTSIDE the bounds (start < workingHour.startTime || end > workingHour.endTime), and if found, returns false. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:106 — [P1, confidence 100] `dateOverrides.find((date) =>` rejects a slot when it is outside any same-day override instead of accepting it when contained by one, so two disjoint override windows suppress every legitimate slot and make the organizer appear unavailable all day.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a logic flaw. Looking at lines 103-127, the code uses `dateOverrides.find()` which returns truthy when ANY override matches the rejection conditions (slot outside that override's time range). With multiple disjoint overrides on the same day, a slot that falls within one override would still be rejected because it falls outside the OTHER override. The logic should accept a slot if it's contained by ANY override, not reject it if it's outside ANY override. The `find()` returns true when the slot is outside an override's bounds, causing `return false` (unavailable), which is inverted logic.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that on line 114, the code compares two dayjs objects using `===` operator: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes') === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, 'minutes')`. In JavaScript, comparing two distinct dayjs objects with `===` compares object references, not their values, so this will always return false even when the dates represent the same instant. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:123 — [P1, confidence 75] `slotStartTime.isAfter(dayjs(date.end)` checks only whether the start is past the override and omits the slot end, so a multi-host candidate that starts inside but finishes after the host's override is published as bookable despite that host being unavailable for the full event.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a logic issue in the date override checking code. Looking at line 123 in the diff: `if (slotStartTime.isAfter(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")))` - this only checks if the slot START time is after the override end. For events with duration (eventLength), if a slot starts inside the override window but the slot END (slotStartTime + eventLength) extends past the override end, the slot would still be considered available. The code checks slotEndTime against the override start (lines 115-119) but only checks slotStartTime against the override end (line 123), creating an asymmetric check that could allow booking slots that extend beyond the host's available override period.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:139 — [P1, confidence 100] `workingHours.find((workingHour) =>` searches for any interval that excludes the slot instead of one interval that contains it, so split working-hour schedules reject all otherwise-valid slots without surfacing an error.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a logic bug in the new code at lines 139-148. The code uses `workingHours.find()` to search for ANY working hour interval where the slot falls outside that interval's bounds (`start < workingHour.startTime || end > workingHour.endTime`). If found, it returns false (slot unavailable). However, this logic is inverted - with multiple working hour intervals (e.g., morning 9-12 and afternoon 2-5), a slot at 10am would be rejected because it falls outside the 2-5pm interval, even though it's valid within the 9-12 interval. The correct logic should check if the slot is contained within ANY working hour interval, not if it falls outside ANY interval.
